title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'équation des lacets' part of the Longue Marche sequel, Grothendieck studies a family of group schemes attached to a pair of indices ρ, σ. These are tori T_ρ, T_σ (two-dimensional, rank-2 tori, very likely maximal tori of GL_2 or of the unit group of a quaternion algebra). Each comes with a norm/determinant to G_m and contains the scalars G_m. From them he builds a 'cube' (117) of groups: R, SR, M, T, M^+, T^+ and their neutral components or degree-0 versions. On the previous page he notes that some faces of the cube are products with SG, at least after passing to pro-coverings.

The faint top lines finish a remark. It would have been 'delectable' to see the four squares of some faces (and of the two other adjacent faces) be cartesian and cocartesian; regrettably they are not.

Then, 'to finish these exercises (gammes) on the radicals', he constructs a canonical homomorphism (118) i_R : G_m → R°_{ρ,σ}. He does this through a canonical homomorphism (119):
- i_τ : G_m → τ°_{ρ,σ} ≅ T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ, λ ↦ (λ, λ). Here the fibre product is taken over the norm maps, and λ is a scalar in each torus.
- Composing with the common norm y : τ° → G_m gives λ ↦ λ², since a scalar in a rank-2 torus has norm λ².

The 'radical' R_{ρ,σ} is described in (105), cf. (104), as a fibre product over τ_{ρ,σ}. Reading this together with the next page, R° is the square-root cover of the norm: R° ≅ τ° ×_{y, G_m, λ↦λ²} G_m, i.e. pairs (t, μ) with y(t) = μ². By the universal property there is then a unique lift i_R(λ) = ((λ, λ), λ), making diagram (120) commute.

The next page draws the consequences:
- (121) is a map of exact sequences built on 1 → μ_2 → G_m → G_m → 1.
- The projection R° → G_m, (t, μ) ↦ μ, composed with i_R is the identity (122).
- This yields direct-product splittings (123): R ≅ SR × G_m and R° ≅ SR° × G_m ≅ ST_ρ × ST_σ × G_m. Grothendieck notes these sharpen his earlier (96).

The problem served is an explicit structural description of these auxiliary 'radical' group schemes, presumably used later for the loop equation / tori in GL_2 over Z or a base.
errors: The only implicit assumption is that the scalars G_m sit in each T_ρ with norm λ ↦ λ². This holds for rank-2 tori in GL_2 or in quaternion units, where the norm is the determinant or reduced norm.
The uniqueness of i_R follows from the universal property of the fibre product.

ideas.what: Diagonal embedding of scalars G_m into the fibre product T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ of two tori over their norms; it composes with the norm to give squaring.
ideas.modern_name: Central scalar subtorus in a fibre product of norm tori

ideas.what: Lifting the scalar embedding to the 'radical' (square-root-of-norm cover) via the universal property of the fibre product. This splits off G_m as a direct factor: R° ≅ SR° × G_m.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of a μ_2-extension (square-root cover of the norm) by a section

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping on auxiliary group schemes: a canonical section and the resulting product decomposition. It is internal to the unpublished development, with no new idea or connection on this page.
transcription_corrections: Top faint lines read roughly: 'délectable de voir dans les quatre carrés des faces s.-p. et inférieures [?] des deux autres accolées cartésiens et cocartésiens, ce qu'ils n'étaient pas [...], regrettablement'. Not 'réjouissances' or 'contiguïs/noncontiguïs'.
In (119) the target factors are written with a bold T: T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ (the torus T_ρ), and τ°_{ρ,σ} is Grothendieck's script T (𝒯°_{ρ,σ}).
The insertions '(104)' and '(105)' together with 'en termes de 𝒯_{ρ,σ}' are marginal additions above the line; the transcription places them correctly in substance.
